locations.name: Carnegie Hall
locations.factShort: Tchaikovsky conducted at its opening in 1891. It was nearly demolished for an office tower in 1960 until the violinist Isaac Stern led a campaign that got the city to buy it.

locations.name: Jane's Carousel
locations.factShort: A 1922 Ohio carousel bought at auction and restored horse by horse over twenty-odd years by the woman it is named for. Its glass pavilion sat in floodwater during Sandy with the carousel dry inside.

locations.name: King Manor
locations.factShort: Rufus King signed the Constitution, was one of the first senators from New York, and argued against slavery's extension from this farmhouse. His son later became governor of the state.

locations.name: The Hunts Point Market
locations.factShort: The largest food distribution centre in the world by some measures, moving several billion dollars of produce, meat and fish a year across three hundred acres. Most of what New York eats passes through here overnight.

locations.name: Floyd Bennett Field
locations.factShort: New York's first municipal airport, which failed commercially because it was too far from Manhattan, then became a record-setting field — Howard Hughes and Wiley Post both flew from it. Its runways are now cracked and grassed over inside a national park.
